bill.title: MORE USDA Grants Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry.

industries.rationale: The bill expands access to USDA rural development grants that support farming communities and agribusiness infrastructure in qualifying counties.
The bill specifically includes Distance Learning and Telemedicine Grants, which fund broadband and telecommunications infrastructure in rural areas.
Community Facilities grants often fund construction of public buildings and infrastructure, creating demand for contractors in eligible counties.

bill.plainSummary: This bill makes it easier for local and tribal governments in rural counties where the federal government owns more than half the land to access certain USDA grant programs. It cuts their required matching funds in half, gives them priority if they haven't received grants in the past decade, and directs USDA to provide extra technical help and flexibility during the application process. The grants cover rural business development, community facilities, telemedicine, and other rural development programs.

plain.whoItTouches: Farmers, and anyone who buys food.

bill.title: Strategic Grazing to Reduce Risk of Wildfire Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 495.

industries.rationale: The bill directly expands grazing opportunities for ranchers and livestock operators on federal lands as part of wildfire management programs.

It directs federal land management agencies to develop and implement strategic grazing programs in areas identified as high wildfire hazard zones. The bill aims to integrate grazing into broader wildfire prevention and forest management strategies on public lands.

bill.title: Combating Organized Retail Crime Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: The bill directly addresses organized theft targeting retail operations and e-commerce platforms.
The bill explicitly covers theft from interstate and foreign shipments, affecting logistics and shipping companies.
The bill addresses online marketplaces and social media platforms where stolen goods are sold, potentially creating new compliance obligations.
The bill expands money laundering statutes to cover prepaid cards and gift cards, affecting payment processors and card issuers.

bill.plainSummary: This bill expands federal authority to prosecute organized retail theft and supply-chain crime. It allows prosecutors to aggregate the value of stolen goods over a 12-month period to meet felony thresholds, makes these offenses predicate crimes for money laundering charges, and authorizes asset forfeiture. The bill also creates a temporary coordination center within the Department of Homeland Security to help federal agencies work together on these cases.

bill.title: A joint resolution proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States relating to contributions and expenditures intended to affect elections.
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: Organizations that spend money to influence elections would face new potential restrictions on their expenditures and fundraising.
The amendment would create new constitutional authority to regulate campaign finance, directly affecting election law practice and lobbying activity.
Limits on campaign spending could affect demand for political advertising across broadcast, digital, and print media platforms.
The amendment's authorization to distinguish between natural persons and corporations could affect how financial institutions participate in election-related spending.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution proposes a constitutional amendment that would allow Congress and state governments to set limits on how much money candidates and others can raise and spend to influence elections. It would also permit lawmakers to treat corporations and other legal entities differently from individual people, including by prohibiting those entities from spending money on elections. The amendment would require ratification by three-fourths of the states to take effect.

bill.title: A joint resolution to direct the removal of United States Armed Forces from hostilities within or against Venezuela that have not been authorized by Congress.
bill.latestActionText: Point of order that the measure is not entitled to expedited procedures under 50 U.S.C. 1546(a) raised against the measure agreed to in Senate by Yea-Nay Vote. 50 - 50. Record Vote Number: 9.

industries.rationale: The resolution would directly affect the deployment and operational scope of U.S. Armed Forces and defense contractors supporting military operations in the Venezuela region.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would require the President to end any U.S. military operations in or against Venezuela unless Congress has formally declared war or authorized the use of force. It preserves the President's authority to defend the United States from an armed attack or imminent threat. The measure addresses congressional oversight of military deployments and the constitutional division of war powers.

plain.whoItTouches: Mostly people outside the United States. It reaches most readers here only indirectly.

bill.title: HALT Fentanyl Act
bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-26.

industries.rationale: The bill changes registration and licensing requirements for pharmaceutical researchers conducting controlled substance research and affects the regulatory classification of chemical substances.
The bill establishes new criminal penalties and quantity thresholds that will affect prosecution and defense of drug trafficking cases.
Universities and research institutions conducting controlled substance research would be subject to the new registration processes and requirements established by the bill.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would permanently classify all fentanyl-related substances as Schedule I controlled substances, meaning they would be treated as having high abuse potential and no accepted medical use. It sets the same criminal penalties and quantity thresholds for fentanyl-related substances as currently apply to fentanyl analogues. The bill also creates a streamlined registration process for researchers studying Schedule I substances and relaxes some requirements for research facilities working with controlled substances.

plain.whoItTouches: People caught up in the criminal law, and victims of crime.

bill.title: A joint resolution terminating the national emergency declared to impose duties on articles imported from Brazil.
bill.latestActionText: Held at the desk.
subjects: Presidents and presidential powers, Vice Presidents

industries.rationale: Manufacturers importing Brazilian goods or components would see tariff costs change if the emergency and its 40% duty are terminated.
Retailers and consumer-goods companies importing products from Brazil would face different import costs depending on whether the tariff remains.
Agricultural importers bringing in Brazilian food products would be affected by the removal or continuation of the 40% tariff.
Importers of Brazilian metals and minerals face tariff exposure, though precious metals were already exempted from the additional duty.

bill.plainSummary: This resolution would end the national emergency that President Trump declared on July 30, 2025, which allowed the imposition of an additional 40% tariff on most goods imported from Brazil. Ending the emergency would remove the legal basis for those extra tariffs. Certain products—including aircraft parts, wood pulp, precious metals, energy products, and fertilizers—were already exempt from the additional tariff.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who buys imported goods, and people who make goods here.

bill.title: TAKE IT DOWN Act
bill.latestActionText: Became Public Law No: 119-12.

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new content moderation obligations and 48-hour removal requirements on social media platforms and user-generated content websites.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would make it a federal crime to publish intimate images or videos of someone online without their consent, including computer-generated deepfakes, when the publication is intended to cause harm or involves a minor. Social media platforms and similar websites would be required to remove such content within 48 hours after receiving a complaint from the person depicted. Violators would face criminal penalties including prison time, fines, and mandatory restitution to victims.

bill.title: Sloan Canyon Conservation and Lateral Pipeline Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.

industries.rationale: The bill directly grants pipeline rights-of-way to a water authority for constructing and operating water transmission infrastructure.
The bill authorizes construction of a water pipeline and related facilities, including geotechnical investigations and tunneling work.
The bill permits excavation and disposal of sand, gravel, minerals, and other materials encountered during pipeline tunneling.

bill.plainSummary: This bill expands the Sloan Canyon National Conservation Area in Nevada by approximately 9,290 acres and grants the Southern Nevada Water Authority rights-of-way to build and operate a water transmission pipeline through the conservation area and other federal land. The pipeline cannot run through designated wilderness areas or permanently harm surface resources in the conservation area. The bill also allows the water authority to excavate and dispose of materials encountered during tunneling, with disposal sites to be identified on federal land through an agreement with the Bureau of Land Management.

bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 474.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects federal payments to county and local governments that host tax-exempt federal lands.
Counties with significant federal land often host mining operations on those lands, and changes to local revenue formulas may indirectly affect permitting and local fiscal capacity.
Federal lands in small counties frequently include oil, gas, or coal extraction sites, and local revenue changes may affect the fiscal environment for these operations.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would modify federal payments to local governments that contain tax-exempt federal land. Specifically, it appears to adjust the Payment in Lieu of Taxes (PILT) formula for small counties, which compensates localities for property-tax revenue they cannot collect on federally owned land. Without access to the bill text, the precise nature of the change to the formula or eligibility criteria cannot be described.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who pays federal tax.

districtAwards.description: THE PROJECT INCLUDES ROW ACQUISITION, FINAL DESIGN, CONSTRUCTION, AND ROLLING STOCK FOR A NEW ALL-ELECTRIC HIGH-SPEED RAIL SYSTEM BETWEEN LAS VEGAS, NV AND RANCHO CUCAMONGA, CA. IT INCLUDES 218 MILES OF TRACK AND SYSTEMS, BRIDGES, HIGHWAY MODIFICATIONS, STATIONS AT LAS VEGAS AND RANCHO CUCAMONGA, A VMF MOW FACILITY IN SLOANE, NV, A MOW FACILITY IN VICTOR VALLEY, CA, AND PROCUREMENT OF 10 HIGH-SPEED TRAINSETS. THE PROJECT WILL SERVE PASSENGERS IN NEVADA AND SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA, AND WILL CONNECT TO THE HIGH DESERT CORRIDOR, METROLINK, AND CALIFORNIA HIGH-SPEED RAIL. BRIGHTLINE WEST, THE SUBRECIPIENT, WILL FINANCE, DESIGN, CONSTRUCT, OPERATE, AND MAINTAIN THE SYSTEM.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
